mechanism_narrative: The recent week-on-week increase in RETAIL_REC mobility, moving from -13.0% to -5.3%, indicates a sustained, albeit gradual, recovery in consumer activity that will continue to drive retail and recreation footfall upwards over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: The mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than the mean RETAIL_REC over the last 28 days, despite the recent upward movement.

mechanism_narrative: A significant rebound in WORKPLACES mobility, specifically the 21-point increase from t-1w (-36.7%) to t-0w (-15.7%), signals a strong return to office-based work, which will directly boost weekday retail and recreation activity over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises by more than 20 points week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not show a significant increase over the next two weeks, despite WORKPLACES maintaining or increasing its rebound.

mechanism_narrative: The concurrent decrease in RESIDENTIAL mobility from t-1w (7.0%) to t-0w (3.9%) and increase in TRANSIT mobility from t-1w (-34.4%) to t-0w (-26.9%) indicates a collective shift towards out-of-home activities and commuting, which will drive higher RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mobility declines or remains stagnant over the next four weeks, even if RESIDENTIAL continues to fall and TRANSIT continues to rise.

mechanism_narrative: The sharp drop in PARKS mobility from t-1w (9.9%) to t-0w (-5.6%) suggests a shift away from outdoor leisure, potentially due to unfavorable weather or other seasonal factors, which will divert recreational spending towards indoor retail and recreation venues over the next week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS mobility drops by more than 10 points week-on-week after a positive week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mobility does not increase over the next week, or PARKS mobility quickly rebounds, indicating a temporary anomaly rather than a sustained shift.

mechanism_narrative: A consistent decline in RESIDENTIAL mobility from its recent peak at t-1w (7.0%) to t-0w (3.9%) signifies a broader trend of people spending less time at home, directly translating to increased engagement in out-of-home activities, including retail and recreation, over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL mobility reverses its trend and increases significantly, or RETAIL_REC does not show a corresponding increase over the next four weeks.

mechanism_narrative: The week-on-week increase in TRANSIT mobility from -34.4% to -26.9% indicates a growing comfort and necessity for public transport, suggesting increased movement across the city for various purposes, which will contribute to higher RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises by more than 5 points week-on-week
failure_condition: TRANSIT mobility declines again in the subsequent week, or RETAIL_REC does not improve despite sustained or increased transit usage.

mechanism_narrative: The simultaneous recovery in WORKPLACES mobility and positive GROCERY_PHARM mobility at t-0w suggests a return to more structured daily routines that combine work and essential errands, creating spillover effects that will boost RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not improve, or either WORKPLACES or GROCERY_PHARM mobility declines significantly over the next four weeks.

mechanism_narrative: Despite overall low mobility indices, the recent upward trend in RETAIL_REC and WORKPLACES from their t-1w lows suggests a cautious but persistent return to out-of-home activities, indicating a slow but steady recovery in consumer confidence and engagement over the next four weeks.
